chunk_map.heading: The instructions are one suspect; your question is another

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
rules_evaluated.evidence: L4: "They are one suspect." is the nearest to violating; 'They' resolves to 'the agent's instructions' in the same sentence, 'each' (L4) to the suspects listed L6-8 in the same chunk, 'your digest' is the reader's own artefact and the header names the instructions. Harm (unresolvable referent) absent.
No other file pointed at by position; grep of body for 'lecture|opening|earlier|module' returns nothing. Nearest: L4 'your digest' names a reader artefact, not a file.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Every backward reference points at a beat that exists.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Nearest: L6 'Open your agreed list of sources' and L7 'Read your brief again' point at the reader's own artefacts. They are instruction-to-open, not 'the X you did/saw'. Host lecture apt101-why-it-agreed includes this slide after it-found-what-you-asked; digest slides precede it.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Live-demo beats survive a text read.

rules_evaluated.evidence: L4 carries the claim (instructions are one suspect among three) with three checks and a next move; self-carrying.

Header 'The instructions are one suspect; your question is another' vs body L4 'They are one suspect', L8 'Your question'. Closest: body also lists a third suspect (the material, L6) the header omits; omission is not contradiction, so the header stays true.

No 'Not X. Not Y. Z.'; L6-8 triple differ in content (each has its own checks) and are not anaphora; L10 'Ask… Then rerun…' two sentences; no superlatives, number+retraction, abstraction stacks or empty verb triplets. Nearest: L6-8 'Fix the material / Fix the instructions' pair, third leg replaced by a different move.
